The spec itself may be part of the problem. `Lod.selection` used to say "Selection runs once per frame per tree", which is the 2,434-trees-per-frame behaviour in your report. I replaced it.

**Which trees get re-selected** (new `Lod.activeSet`):
- **Cells:** trees are grouped into cells along the stage. Each cell knows the range of screen heights its trees can have from the camera's position.
- **Active trees:** a tree is re-selected each frame only while it's within its hysteresis margin of a level threshold or of the 120 m full-detail line, or while it's fading. Every other tree is settled and draws from its cell's static batch with no per-frame CPU work.
- **Rechecking cells:** a settled cell records how far the camera can move, or how much it can zoom, before any of its trees could reach a margin. It's checked again only after that.
- **GPU-side work:** sprite thinning and wind are worked out on the GPU, so they never make a tree active. My guess is that one of these is what's making nearly every tree active now.
- **Moving between the two:** a tree switches between the active list and the static batch without rebuilding the batch or reallocating a buffer.
- **Expected count:** at most a few hundred active trees per frame on a normal run, shown in the stats overlay.

**The 300–400 ms spikes** (new `Performance.frameStability`): with tree CPU time staying at 1–1.5 ms during a spike, the frame is probably waiting on something other than tree code. The spec now rules out the usual suspects:
- **No waiting on the GPU:** counters, timestamps and culling results are read back at least two frames after they're written, from a ring of buffers. There is never a blocking map or a wait-for-idle.
- **Pipelines and shaders:** every one the trees can use, for every level, pass, cascade, fade and debug mode, is created at stage load.
- **Buffers:** instance, indirect-draw and fade buffers are allocated once at load at full size. They're never resized during a run, and only changed entries are uploaded.
- **Disk and worker threads:** nothing in the tree system touches the disk or picks up worker results on the main thread during a run.

**GPU cost:** occlusion culling, the sprite depth pre-pass and the shadow cascade rules were already in the spec. `Performance.mitigations` now adds that every mitigation is on by default at every quality setting, and only a debug toggle can turn one off.

**Reporting:**
- **Stats overlay:** now also shows how many trees were re-selected, how many drew from static batches, how many cells were checked, and which mitigations are on.
- **Benchmark file:** records the machine name, which mitigations were on, average and peak re-selection counts, and tree main-pass and shadow-pass GPU time separately.
- **Spike frames:** any frame slower than three times the average is logged with its CPU and GPU time, the tree share, and any pipeline creation, buffer allocation or upload, or GPU readback in that frame.
- **Comparing runs:** a run can be compared with an earlier results file, which gives the before and after for each fix.
- **New budget rule:** no frame may take more than three times the average because of tree work.

The budget still assumes the game's minimum-spec GPU at 1080p. I don't know if the Radeon 890M at 2117×1018 is your minimum-spec machine. If it isn't, the 1 ms target doesn't strictly apply on jackie, but the code step should still aim for it.

**What changed in the spec:**
- **`spec/trees/Lod.pi`:** `selection` no longer re-selects every tree every frame, and a new `activeSet` section was added.
- **`spec/trees/Performance.pi`:** `counters`, `benchmark`, `budget` and `mitigations` were extended, and a new `frameStability` section was added.

**Anchors the code should follow, in this order:**
1. `Lod.activeSet` and `Lod.selection` in `.claude/reference/trees/Lod.md`: find why nearly every tree is active, and fix it.
2. `Performance.frameStability` in `.claude/reference/trees/Performance.md`: use the spike-frame log to find what causes the 300–400 ms frames, and remove it.
3. `Performance.mitigations` in `.claude/reference/trees/Performance.md`, `Drawing.culling` in `.claude/reference/trees/Drawing.md`, and `Lod.shadows` in `.claude/reference/trees/Lod.md`: turn on occlusion culling, the sprite depth pre-pass and the cascade rules.

Run the benchmark on jackie at medium quality before and after each of these, and report the comparison from `Performance.benchmark` against `Performance.budget`.

## Selection

- The level is chosen by the tree's projected height on screen, not by raw distance, so a change of camera field of view, as between the chase and the bonnet camera, picks the right level.
- Projected height is measured from the tree's bounding sphere and the camera's position and field of view before camera shake and bounce are applied, so a shaking camera does not push trees back and forth across a threshold.
- Each threshold has hysteresis. A tree moves to a coarser level when it drops below the threshold, and back to the finer one only when it rises above the threshold by a margin, 15% of the threshold by default.
- The default thresholds are pushed far out, so a player near a tree only ever sees it at full detail. Sprite thinning starts below 6% of the screen height, branches move from LOD0 to LOD1 below 2.5%, and the tree moves to the impostor below 1%. For a 15 m tree at a 60 degree vertical field of view, that is roughly 215 m, 520 m and 1300 m.
- A tree within 120 m of the camera is always drawn at LOD0 with every sprite at full size, whatever its projected height, the field of view or the graphics quality setting.
- Selection depends only on the frame's camera, never on draw order, culling batches or which pass is drawing.
- Selection is not re-run for every tree every frame; see activeSet.

## Active Set

- Trees are grouped into cells along the stage. For each cell, the camera's distance range to the cell's trees bounds the projected height each of them can have, so whole cells can be settled at one level.
- A tree is active, and re-selected on the CPU each frame, only while its projected height is within its hysteresis margin of a threshold, or of the 120 m full-detail distance, or while it is in a fade. Every other tree is settled and drawn from its cell's static batch for its level, with no per-frame CPU work.
- A settled cell records how far the camera can move, and how much the field of view can change, before any of its trees could reach a margin. The cell is checked again only once the camera has moved or zoomed that much, not every frame.
- On a normal benchmark run, at most a few hundred trees are active in any frame, and the tree stats overlay reports the count.
- Sprite thinning ([Foliage.simplification](./Foliage.md#simplification)) and wind are computed per sprite on the GPU from the camera. They never make a tree active.
- A tree that becomes active or settled moves between the static batch and the active list without rebuilding the cell's batch from scratch or reallocating a buffer.

## Counters

- A tree stats overlay, shown with the [Lod.debugView](./Lod.md#debug-view) toggle, reports per frame the number of trees drawn at each level and in a fade, the number of foliage sprites drawn, the triangles and draw calls of the tree passes, shadow passes included, and the GPU time of the tree main pass and tree shadow pass on their own.
- It also reports the CPU time of level selection and fade updates per frame, the number of trees re-selected that frame, the number drawn from static batches, and the number of cells checked ([Lod.activeSet](./Lod.md#active-set)).
- It shows which mitigations are on: occlusion culling, the sprite depth prepass, the shadow cascade rules and sprite thinning.
- At stage load it records the time spent deriving, meshing and baking variants, how many came from the disk cache, and the GPU and disk memory the variants use.

## Benchmark

- A benchmark runs a fixed camera path along a stage with the procedural trees and reports the average, 1% low and worst frame time, the tree GPU time and the stage load time.
- It can run the same path with trees turned off, so the trees' own cost is the difference between the two runs.
- Results are written to a file with the stage, graphics quality setting, resolution, GPU and machine name, so runs can be compared. The file also records which mitigations were on, the average and peak number of re-selected trees, and the tree main pass and tree shadow pass GPU times separately.
- Every frame slower than three times the run's average is listed in the file with its frame number, its CPU and GPU time, the tree CPU and GPU time, and any pipeline or shader creation, buffer allocation or upload, or GPU readback that happened in it.
- A run can be compared with an earlier result file, and the comparison prints the change in every figure, so the effect of each fix is shown on its own.

## Budget

- The trees' cost is negligible: on the benchmark, at the game's minimum-spec GPU, 1080p and medium quality, trees add at most 1.0 ms to the average GPU frame time and at most 1.0 ms to the 1% low, compared with the same path with no trees.
- Level selection and fade updates take at most 0.1 ms of main-thread CPU time per frame.
- Players never wait for tree generation: with the shipped cache, trees add at most 0.5 s to a stage's load time compared with the same stage with no trees.
- No frame spikes because of trees: during a run, no frame takes more than three times the average because of tree work.
- A run over budget is a failing result in the benchmark's output file.

## Frame Stability

- The tree code never waits on the GPU during a frame. Counters, timestamps, culling results and anything else read back from the GPU are read at least two frames after they were written, from buffers in a ring, and never with a blocking map or a wait-for-idle.
- Every pipeline and shader the trees can use, for every level, pass, cascade, fade and debug mode, is created or warmed at stage load, so none is compiled the first time a tree reaches a new level or pass.
- Instance, indirect-argument and fade buffers are allocated at stage load at their largest size for the stage, and are never resized, reallocated or fully re-uploaded during a run. Per-frame changes upload only the entries that changed.
- Cache reads and any variant generation finish before the stage starts; nothing in the tree system touches the disk or a worker queue's results on the main thread during a run.

## Mitigations

- Every mitigation below is on by default at every graphics quality setting. Only a debug toggle may turn one off, and the benchmark records it.
- Foliage overdraw. Each atlas cluster image has a tight polygon of 6 to 8 vertices around its opaque part, and sprites use it instead of a full quad, so few pixels are spent on texels that fail the alpha test. Foliage sprites draw in a depth-only pass first and are then shaded only where their depth is equal, so each covered pixel is shaded once; both passes compute positions identically ([Foliage.wind](./Foliage.md#wind)). Sprite thinning past 120 m ([Foliage.simplification](./Foliage.md#simplification)) cuts the sprite count of distant crowns.
- Culling. Each frame, instances are culled against the view frustum and against a hierarchical depth buffer built from the previous frame's terrain and trees, on the GPU, and the survivors are compacted into indirect draws. A tree hidden behind a hill or a closer stand of trees costs neither vertices nor pixels.
- Draw calls. Every impostor of every species shares one texture array and draws in a single instanced call.
- Foliage shading. Leaf translucency is a cheap wrap-lighting term from the atlas thickness map, not a ray march or extra light lookup; ambient occlusion stays baked. No foliage shader samples more than its three atlas textures plus the shadow map.
- Geometry. LOD0 branches of a variant have at most 6,000 triangles for a conifer or broadleaf and 2,000 for a shrub, and a crown has at most 600 sprites, 200 for a shrub.
- Fades. At most 32 trees fade at once; a tree whose level changes while that many are fading switches at its next free slot, still with a full fade.
- Shadows. Tree shadow casting follows [Lod.shadows](./Lod.md#shadows).
- Load. The cache is generated when the game is built and shipped with it ([Placement.caching](./Placement.md#caching)).

## Hotspots
## Shadows

- Shadows use one level coarser than the one drawn, and never the impostor within the near shadow cascade.
- Only the nearest shadow cascade draws trees with wind and every sprite. Farther cascades draw trees as LOD1 with thinned sprites, or the impostor, with no wind, and re-render their tree casters every fourth frame, the cascades staggered so no two re-render on the same frame.
- Shadow casters are culled per cascade, on the GPU, like the main pass.
- Shadow casters are never dithered. A tree's shadow level switches once, when its fade finishes, so its shadow does not flicker while the tree fades.

## Budget

content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The work runs as a chain of Suspense prompts. Each prompt begins with a <task-instructions> block, and these rules apply:
   - **Understanding file:** write the task's constraints to `.suspense/history/<id>.understanding.md` before changing anything. It is a Markdown list only, at most 12 lines, each a link to `.claude/reference/...`.
   - **Spec:** read the compiled reference under `.claude/reference`. Never read or change `./spec`.
   - **Disagreements:** follow the spec, and say in the reply where it and the prompt disagree.
   - **Spec-step claims:** every spec step so far has wrongly claimed `src/` is empty. The game is in `src/games/rally`.

   Overall goal: replace the rally game's trees with procedural L-system trees, with clean LOD transitions and lush, lightweight foliage, plus all the follow-up fixes.

   The current prompt (task id 1791398294-FixTreePerformanceRegression2) says, verbatim: "The tree benchmark on jackie at medium quality (Radeon 890M, 2117x1018) fails badly: trees add 38 ms to the average frame and 88 ms to the 1% low against a 1 ms budget, level selection takes 1.34 ms against 0.1 ms, and some frames spike to 300-400 ms while tree CPU work stays around 1-1.5 ms. The report shows 2,434 trees re-selected per frame, so almost every tree goes through the per-frame path instead of the static batches. Find out why so many trees are active and fix it, so only trees near a level threshold or in a fade are re-selected each frame. Find the cause of the 300-400 ms spikes and remove it. Then cut the GPU cost of the tree main and shadow passes toward the budget in .claude/reference/trees/Performance.md, using the mitigations it lists that are missing or turned off now: occlusion culling, the sprite depth prepass and the shadow cascade rules in .claude/reference/trees/Lod.md#shadows. Report the benchmark numbers before and after each fix."

   The spec anchors to follow are: `Lod.activeSet`, `Lod.selection`, `Performance.frameStability`, `Performance.mitigations`, `Drawing.culling`, `Lod.shadows`, `Performance.benchmark` and `Performance.budget`.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Stack:** three.js r186 with WebGL2, rsbuild, rstest, rslint, TypeScript.
   - **Shaders:** InstancedMesh batches, with tree code injected into standard, depth and basic materials through `onBeforeCompile`.
   - **Determinism:** L-system grammar and skeleton use their own PRNG and trig (`tsin`, `tcos`).
   - **Levels:** LOD0 branches, LOD1 trunk plus first-order limbs, and the impostor (level 2). The impostor is an octahedral texture array with 3 layers per variant and one draw call for all impostors.
   - **Foliage sprites:** a per-kind atlas of 8 cluster images (`leaftex.ts`). Sprites face the camera, are thinned in the shader from projected height (`treeLod` attribute), and drawn from keep-fraction buckets `KEEP = [1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.45, 0.3]` using draw ranges.
   - **Selection and fades:** per-tree fade state (`stepFade`, `selectLevel`, `spriteRole`), `MAX_FADES = 32`, hysteresis 15%, `FULL_DETAIL_DISTANCE = 120`. Thresholds `[0.06, 0.025, 0.01]` mean thinning start, LOD0→1, and LOD1→impostor.
   - **Batching:** a static/active split built by a time-sliced job. The job runs every `rebuildDistance` (5 m) with `move = rebuild + 4`. `ZOOM_MARGIN = 1.025` is the cause of the large active shells.
   - **Lighting:** sky diffuse light as spherical harmonics (`setTreeSky`), dither as an 8×8 Bayer pattern.
   - **Sprite pre-pass:** opt-in via `?treeprepass=1`. Debug modes are 0–5.
   - **Benchmark:** `__rally.treeBenchmark()`. Frames are timed with `gl.finish` and the GPU timer off; a separate pass takes the GPU timer queries.
   - **Verification:** headless Chromium on the real GPU (Radeon 890M) over CDP, with `--use-angle=gl-egl`.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `.suspense/history/1791398294-FixTreePerformanceRegression2.understanding.md` holds 12 constraints:
     - active-set rule
     - cells and recheck slack
     - thinning and wind never activate a tree; a few hundred active
     - no rebuild or reallocation when trees move between lists
     - no GPU waits
     - pipelines warmed and buffers preallocated at load
     - overlay counters
     - benchmark file contents
     - no frame over 3× the average
     - all mitigations on by default
     - cascade rules
     - two-phase occlusion culling
   - **`src/games/rally/trees/stats.ts`**
     - `TreeFrameStats` gained `statics`, `cellsChecked`, `allocs`, `uploadBytes`, `repacks` and `commit`.
     - `TreeGpuTimer` gained `mainSamples` and `shadowSamples`, plus a `takePassSamples()` method.
   - **`src/games/rally/trees/draw.ts`** (the `TreeRenderer`)
     - `ensureCapacity` now counts allocations, `upload` adds `(n - from) * 28 * 4` bytes, `pack` counts re-packs, and a commit sets `current.commit`.
     - `mitigations()` currently reports `{ occlusionCulling: false, spritePrepass: SPRITE_PREPASS, shadowCascadeRules: true, spriteThinning: true }`.
     - New `prewarm(camera?)` and `settle()`:
       ```ts
       prewarm(camera?: PerspectiveCamera): void { const at=new Vector3(); if(camera) camera.getWorldDirection(at).multiplyScalar(30).add(camera.position);
         const m=new Matrix4().setPosition(at).elements;
         const one=(b:Batch)=>{ this.ensureCapacity(b,1); b.mat.set(m,0); b.inst.set([0,1,0,0],0); b.fade.set([1,SOLID,1,0],0); b.lod.set([5,10,0.06,0.01],0); for(const a of [b.aMat!,b.aInst!,b.aFade!,b.aLod!]){a.clearUpdateRanges(); a.needsUpdate=true;} for(const mesh of b.meshes){mesh.count=1; mesh.visible=true;} };
         for (const lv of this.library.all()) for (const part of [0,1,...SPRITE_PARTS]) { one(this.dynamicBatch(lv,part)); one(this.staticBatch(lv,part)); } one(this.impostorBatch()); }
       settle(): void { for (const b of this.dynamic.values()) { b.count=0; this.upload(b,0);} for (const b of this.statics.values()) this.packStatic(b); this.packImpostors(); this.upload(this.impostorBatch(), this.impostorBatch().count); }
       ```
     - The static test in `rebuild` still uses `ZOOM_MARGIN = 1.025` and `move = (rebuildDistance ?? 5) + 4`, through `hMin`/`hMax` and the `steadyLevel` condition. This is the planned active-set fix target.
     - `SPRITE_PREPASS` is true only with `?treeprepass=1`. `PREPASS_ORDER` is -10. View culling re-packs the static batches when the camera turns more than 8° (`REPACK`).
   - **`src/games/rally/game/tree-bench.ts`**
     - New `SpikeFrame` type with `frame`, `ms`, `cpuMs`, `gpuWaitMs`, `steps`, `treeCpuMs`, `programs`, `allocs`, `uploadBytes`, `repacks` and `commit`.
     - `BenchRun` gained `active`, `activePeak`, `treeMainGpuMs`, `treeShadowGpuMs` and `spikes`.
     - `TreeBenchReport` gained `machine`, `mitigations` and `comparison`.
     - New `compareReports()` and `figures()` functions.
     - `checkBudget` now fails a run that has more spike frames with trees than without.
   - **`src/games/rally/game/rally-game.ts`**
     - `treeBenchmark` options now include `compare` and `machine`.
     - It records a per-frame `detail` (with `renderer.info.programs` delta, CPU time vs GPU wait, and `benchSteps`), spikes over 3× the average, active average and peak, and separate pass GPU times.
     - New `benchSteps` record; `benchFrame` laps `terrain`, `scatter`, `trees`, `env` and `render`.
     - The init calls `this.trees.prewarm(this.camera)`.
   - **Earlier files in the module (from previous turns):**
     - `materials.ts`: sprite, prepass, depth and impostor materials, `setSpritePrepassDebug`, the `TREE_VIEW_Z` define, `__treeUniforms`.
     - `mesh.ts` (sprites with `ends`), `leaftex.ts`, `species.ts`, `load.ts`, `impostor.ts`, `overlay.ts`.
     - `engine/environment.ts` (sky SH), `engine/world-shading.ts` (wrap translucency term using `tlThickness`).
     - `pages/map-viewer.ts`: debug select with modes 0–5.
     - `tests/rally/trees.test.ts`: 29 tests passed before this turn.
     - `src/games/rally/DETAILS.md`: docs updated in earlier turns.
   - **Local helpers (not committed):**
     - `.shots/cdp.mjs`: headless GPU Chromium at 2117×1018. Steps are `wait:`, `nav:`, `shot`, `save:<file>=<js>`.
     - `.shots/bench.sh <name> [compare.json]`: runs The Jackie at medium, saves `.shots/<name>.json` and prints a summary.
     - The dev server is running on port 3123 (`rsbuild dev --env-mode noreload`).

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Draw-order bug (previous turn):** caused by the less-or-equal test plus polygon-offset pre-pass. Fixed by making the pre-pass opt-in and the lit pass exact-equal with no depth write.
   - **Depth debug view all white:** a sign error. Changed `TREE_VIEW_Z` to `vViewPosition.z` (impostor: `-tiView.z`).
   - **Background output filling `/tmp`:** happened earlier in the session; avoid large outputs.
   - **`pkill -f "port 3123"` exits with 144:** it kills the calling shell. This is harmless.
   - **Spikes after the warm-up fix:** the warm-up fix (`prewarm` with real instances) did NOT remove the spikes. Run b1 still has 520 ms at frame 8 (render 506 ms), 366 ms at frame 23 on a commit, and 140 ms at frame 4. The root cause is still unknown.

5. Problem Solving:
   - **Baseline benchmarks (Jackie, medium, 2117×1018):**

     | Run | Tree cost (avg) | 1% low | Worst | Tree GPU main / shadow | Selection | Active (peak) | Tree load |
     | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
     | b0 | +29.88 ms | +58.8 ms | 431 ms | 33.45 / 4.76 ms | 0.924 ms | 2,489 (9,612) | 582 ms |
     | b0c (with step breakdown) | +32.28 ms | +74.9 ms | 406.6 ms | 33.31 / 4.66 ms | 0.985 ms | 2,416 (8,966) | 689 ms |
     | b1 (warm-up fix) | +39.35 ms | +77.6 ms | 520 ms | 35.05 / 5.14 ms | 1.096 ms | 1,967 (8,825) | 614 ms |

     - b0 spikes: frame 8 (431 ms); frame 17 (165 ms, a commit with 169 re-packs and a 3.6 MB upload).
     - b0c: the frame-8 spike is CPU time inside `renderer.render` (401 ms), with no new programs or allocations.
     - b1 vs b0c: worse on average and worst frame. Run-to-run variance on this integrated GPU is large.
   - **Active-set diagnosis:** the conservative zoom margin of 2.5% (about ±32 m at 1,300 m) plus the 9 m move margin creates a large ring of active trees at the far thresholds. Planned fix:
     - Drop the zoom margin from the static test.
     - Restart the job when the screen-height scale (`px`) changes by about 1%.
     - Optionally compute exact per-tree slack to the next switching boundary.
     - Expected result: about 500 active trees.
     - Interpretation to report: the spec's "within its hysteresis margin" is read as proximity to the actual switching boundary, since the literal reading gives about 3,000 active trees.
   - **Spike ideas still to check:**
     - The early-frame spikes may relate to the run starting right after the warm-up pass.
     - Shadow-map work, texture uploads (sprite atlas mipmaps), or a driver stall.
     - Job commit and re-pack uploads.
     - Approaches: a CDP CPU profile around frame 8, or timing shadow vs main inside render.
   - **Mitigations still to do:**
     - Turn the sprite pre-pass on by default, with a self-test fallback (render and check for magenta misses).
     - CPU culling of shadow casters against the shadow box, using `worldUniforms.wsShadowBox` and a light-space projection.
     - Occlusion culling: GPU Hi-Z with indirect draws isn't possible in WebGL2. Options are per-cell hardware occlusion queries, or a terrain horizon test.
     - Cascade rules: there is a single shadow map (the near cascade), so the farther-cascade rules have nothing to apply to.

6. All user messages:
   - "We want to replace the trees in the rally game with procedural L-systems that can support clean LOD transitions and more realistic foliage" (twice, the second time with "The spec is brand new on top of an existing codebase, so do your best.").
   - "We're getting some weird flickering and fading out issues"
   - "The LOD should be at a far greater distance.  it's really weird how a tree folliage suddenly changes when we get close to it."
   - "How big a performance his is the new l-system and foliage dealio ?"
   - "So what can you do to make it a negligable hit ?"
   - "There's some super wonky stuff going on with it now.  They're unlit silhouettes basically, and they're "fading in" as a sharp line kinda like a wipe down.  I'm wondering if we could emulate it with spites or what else to make this nice at lush but lightweight."
   - "We're having some draw order issues now."
   - The current prompt, quoted verbatim in section 1.
   - Each prompt carried the task-instructions rules: write the understanding file first; don't read or change `./spec`; follow the spec over the prompt and report disagreements.
   - Standing project constraints from AGENTS.md: public repository; no third-party files; commit only when asked (nothing has been committed); keep docs short. There are no secret-handling instructions beyond those in AGENTS.md.

7. Pending Tasks:
   - Fix the active set so only trees near a switching boundary or fading are re-selected; measure (b2) against b1.
   - Find and remove the 300–500 ms spike cause (CPU time inside `renderer.render` on early frames and commit frames); measure.
   - Mitigations, each measured:
     - sprite pre-pass on by default, with a fallback;
     - shadow caster culling and the cascade rules;
     - occlusion culling, as far as WebGL2 allows (report the deviation).
   - Overlay: show re-selected, static and cells-checked counts and the mitigation states.

   - Final report: benchmark numbers before and after each fix, against the budget, with the deviations stated. Clean up `.shots`, stop the dev server, commit nothing.

8. Current Work:
   I had just run benchmark b1 after adding the warm-up `prewarm(camera)`, which draws one real instance per batch. Output: "b1: avg 43.64 (no trees 4.29) +39.35  1%low 90.2 (+77.6)  worst 520 ... active 1967 peak 8825  spikes 3 ... spike frame 8 ms 520 render 506 ... frame 23 ms 366.6 render 356.6 commit True repacks 169 uploadBytes 3613792 ... frame 4 ms 139.9 render 130.8". So the warm-up fix did not remove the spikes. The next planned change was the active-set fix in `trees/draw.ts` `rebuild()`: remove `ZOOM_MARGIN` from the `hMin`/`hMax` static test and lower the job's zoom retrigger to about 1%.

9. Optional Next Step:
   Do the active-set fix in `src/games/rally/trees/draw.ts`. In the static classification, compute `hMin` and `hMax` without `ZOOM_MARGIN` (or from exact boundary slack), and lower the zoom retrigger threshold to about 1%. content.content:
## Simplification

- Each sprite has a rank, from its prune priority and its seed. Within the full-detail distance every sprite draws at full size.
- Once the tree is outside the full-detail distance and below the thinning threshold ([Lod.selection](./Lod.md#selection)), as its projected height falls toward the impostor threshold, the lowest-ranked sprites shrink smoothly to nothing while the remaining sprites grow, so the area the crown covers on screen stays the same. Sprites are never added or removed at once and never dithered.
- By the impostor threshold a crown has 25% of its sprites, each scaled to keep the crown's coverage.

## Shading

- Sprites are shaded through the game's normal lit path for opaque geometry: the same sun, sky ambient, fog and shadow maps as the terrain. They are never drawn unlit, emissive, with a constant colour or with a zero or missing normal.
- The normal is the normal of the crown's fitted ellipsoid at the sprite's position, bent by the atlas normal map, so the crown shades as one soft volume with leafy detail and the individual sprites do not show.
- Light through leaves is a wrap-lighting term weighted by the thickness map, so a crown against a low sun glows at its edges.
- Sprites receive shadows, including the crown's own shadow, so the inside and the side away from the sun are darker.
- Ambient occlusion is baked per sprite from how deep it sits inside the crown.
- Each tree gets a hue and value variation from its seed, within its species palette.

## Alpha
## Culling

Occlusion culling is two-phase. Trees hidden by the previous frame's depth are tested again against this frame's depth after the first draw, and drawn if visible, so a tree coming out from behind a hill or a closer tree never appears a frame late or flickers.

content.content:
## Alpha

- Atlas textures use coverage-preserving mipmaps. Each mip level's alpha is scaled so the share of texels passing the alpha test matches the full-size texture, so crowns do not thin out or fade away with distance.
- The alpha-test threshold is one fixed value shared by every pass, the shadow pass included.
- Where the renderer has MSAA, foliage uses alpha-to-coverage, so sprite edges do not shimmer.

## Wind

- Sway is hierarchical: the trunk bends, each branch sways about its parent with an amplitude that grows with branch order, and each sprite moves with the branch it hangs from and flutters by a small turn about its view axis.
- Each vertex carries its branch order, its phase and its distance along its branch, baked from the skeleton, and the motion is computed on the GPU from those and a global wind direction and strength.
- Every pass that draws a sprite, the depth pass, the lit pass and the shadow pass, computes its position with the same function from the same inputs, so their depths match exactly.
- The impostor sways as a whole with the trunk motion, so it matches the geometry at the transition.

- Every pass that draws a sprite, the depth pass, the lit pass and the shadow pass, computes its position with the same function from the same inputs, so their depths match exactly.
- The impostor sways as a whole with the trunk motion, so it matches the geometry at the transition.
.claude/reference/trees/Foliage.md:19:- By the impostor threshold a crown has 25% of its sprites, each scaled to keep the crown's coverage.
.claude/reference/trees/Foliage.md:32:- Atlas textures use coverage-preserving mipmaps. Each mip level's alpha is scaled so the share of texels passing the alpha test matches the full-size texture, so crowns do not thin out or fade away with distance.
.claude/reference/trees/Foliage.md:34:- Where the renderer has MSAA, foliage uses alpha-to-coverage, so sprite edges do not shimmer.

content.content:
241	- Trees (`trees/`, L-system species in `trees/species.ts`; map rules keep the old tree type ids): 8 variants per species.
242	  Branches are tubes at two levels (LOD0 = the skeleton without twigs, LOD1 = trunk + first-order limbs), then an
243	  octahedral impostor (albedo, normal + depth, thickness: lit like everything else). Foliage = one lit, camera-facing
244	  cluster sprite per leaf point from a per-kind atlas of 8 images (`trees/leaftex.ts`: albedo, normal + thickness),
245	  drawn with both branch levels; past 120 m and below 6 % of the screen height the lowest-ranked sprites shrink away
246	  while the rest grow (shader), down to 25 % at the impostor (1 %). Branches switch LOD0 -> LOD1 at 2.5 %. Level changes
247	  are a fixed 0.3 s fade per tree (8x8 ordered dither, one fade value per tree, at most 32 at once), selected from the
248	  camera before shake (`CameraRig.steady`) with 15 % hysteresis; settled trees sit in static batches.
249	- Tree shading: sprites / impostors go through the standard lit path (sun, shadows, fog); the sky's diffuse light is
250	  spherical harmonics of the environment (`setTreeSky`, engine/environment.ts) instead of the env map, so they read 2
251	  atlas textures + shadow map + cloud noise. Sprite normals = crown ellipsoid bent by the atlas normal map;
252	  translucency = a wrap term on the thickness map. Caps: LOD0 branches <= 6,000 triangles (shrubs 2,000), <= 600

content.text:
I fixed the active set and found the cause of the 300–400 ms spikes, but the trees are still far over budget: +42.7 ms average frame (+45.4 ms 1% low) against 1 ms, and 0.42 ms selection against 0.1 ms.

**The spikes were a benchmark artefact, not tree work.** In Chrome, `gl.finish()` returns without waiting for the GPU (0 ms on every frame), so benchmark frames queued up. Every few seconds one frame blocked while about 10 queued frames drained (≈10 × 34 ms). On those frames GPU time was a normal 34 ms. I ruled out shader compiles, buffer allocations and uploads, garbage collection and VRAM eviction first. The benchmark now ends each frame with `waitForGpu` (a 1-pixel readback, in the benchmark only). After that change: zero spike frames, worst frame 70.8 ms against a 53.5 ms average. Because of that change, b8 and later aren't comparable with the earlier runs: CPU and GPU no longer overlap, so the average went up.

**Why so many trees were active:**
- **Zoom margin:** the 2.5% zoom allowance made a ~±32 m ring of active trees around each far threshold. It is now 0.4%.
- **120 m and 130 m lines:** every tree near the full-detail or shadow distance was activated. Now LOD0 trees only activate when their level would actually change, and the shader decides the shadow distance per tree.
- **Fade slots:** trees just off-screen took fade slots, because the per-frame view test had a 20° margin. It's exact now.
- **Camera jumps:** after the benchmark's jump back to the start, thousands of trees queued for fades. A move over 50 m now counts as a cut, and every tree takes its level at once.

**Benchmark (The Jackie, medium, 2117×1018), one fix at a time.** b1–b7 are on the old timing:

| Run | Fix | Tree cost (avg) | Main / shadow GPU | Selection | Active (peak) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| b1 | starting point | +39.4 ms | 35.1 / 5.1 ms | 1.10 ms | 1,967 (8,825) |
| b2 | zoom margin | +37.3 | 27.6 / 3.95 | 0.52–0.63 | 887 (8,425) |
| b3 | 120/130 m lines, shadow casters only | +33.2 | 28.6 / **1.4** | 0.635 | 957 (4,807) |
| b4 | exact view test | +26.5 | 29.8 / 1.36 | 0.367 | 536 (8,464) |
| b5 | camera cuts | +29.9 | 32.0 / 1.4 | 0.59 | 905 (1,844) |
| b6 | depth prepass on | +34.1 | 34.0 / 1.48 | 0.526 | 1,064 (2,305) |
| b7 | terrain occlusion | +35.5 | 33.4 / 1.15 | 0.288 | **319 (456)** |
| b8 | real GPU sync, all on | **+42.7**, 1% low 64.6 ms, 0 spikes | 39.0 / 1.09 | 0.416 | 370 (553) |

Run-to-run noise on this integrated GPU is several ms. b5–b7 averages went up, not down: b5 because trees now draw at their correct (finer) levels after a cut, and b6/b7 because the prepass costs more than it saves on this GPU (below).

On the honest timing, each mitigation turned off on its own:

| Off | Avg | 1% low |
|---|---|---|
| none (b8) | +42.7 ms | 64.6 ms |
| prepass | +43.9 ms | 119.5 ms |
| occlusion | +44.2 ms | 152.3 ms |

**Mitigations, all on by default:**
- **Sprite depth prepass:** on by default, `?treeprepass=0` turns it off. The opt-in version was broken on this driver: 36% of sprite pixels missed their EQUAL test, so its earlier speed-up came partly from unshaded pixels. The prepass now uses the lit sprite's own program, and a check at load found 0 misses. If a driver does miss, the check turns the prepass off.
- **Shadows:** the shadow pass draws only casters within the shadow distance. The cascade rules hold for the one shadow map, which is the near cascade. There are no farther cascades for the other rules to apply to.
- **Occlusion culling:** `trees/occlusion.ts`, `?treeocclusion=0` turns it off.
- **Overlay:** shows re-selected trees, static trees, cells checked, trees hidden by terrain, and which mitigations are on.

**Where the spec and the prompt disagree, or the spec can't be met:**
- **Occlusion:** the spec asks for GPU culling against a depth pyramid with indirect draws, two-phase. WebGL2 has neither compute shaders nor indirect draws. I built a conservative CPU version instead: a terrain horizon map per batching job, which only hides trees the terrain blocks from every camera position within 9 m. A brute-force check of thousands of culled trees found no wrong culls. It doesn't account for trees hiding other trees.
- **Prepass:** the spec requires it on, but on the Radeon 890M it costs about 1 ms more on average because the sprite pass is partly vertex-bound. It's kept for the 1% low.
- **Active-set reading:** I read "within its hysteresis margin" as near the actual switching point. Read literally (anywhere in the 15% band), you'd get about 3,000 active trees.
- **Fade cap vs. active count:** with 32 fades of 0.3 s, at most ~107 trees can change level per second. On a dense stage more cross than that, and trees waiting for a slot have to stay active. That is a large part of the remaining ~370.
- **The 1 ms GPU budget can't be met with the spec's thresholds.** The cost is the volume of foliage sprites (about 2M per frame). Bringing the thresholds closer, which `Lod.budget` allows for lower quality settings, gave 15.4 ms average at half distance and 10.4 ms at 0.3×, still not 1 ms. These two runs were on the old timing, so compare them with b7's 38 ms, not b8. Changing medium's thresholds is your call, so I left them alone.
- **Tree load is 0.6 s against 0.5 s,** because no variants came from the cache (0 of 24) during these runs. I didn't change that here.

`DETAILS.md` and the tests are updated. tsc, `npm run test` (506 passed) and lint on `src/` and `tests/` are clean. Prettier reformatted the whole tree module, which hadn't been formatted before. The local `.shots` helpers are deleted and the dev server I started is stopped. Another `rsbuild` process I didn't start is still running, and I left it alone. Nothing is committed.

| Off | Avg | 1% low |

**Mitigations, all on by default:**
- **Sprite depth prepass:** on by default, `?treeprepass=0` turns it off. The opt-in version was broken on this driver: 36% of sprite pixels missed their EQUAL test, so its earlier speed-up came partly from unshaded pixels. The prepass now uses the lit sprite's own program, and a check at load found 0 misses. If a driver does miss, the check turns the prepass off.
- **Shadows:** the shadow pass draws only casters within the shadow distance. The cascade rules hold for the one shadow map, which is the near cascade. There are no farther cascades for the other rules to apply to.
- **Occlusion culling:** `trees/occlusion.ts`, `?treeocclusion=0` turns it off.
- **Overlay:** shows re-selected trees, static trees, cells checked, trees hidden by terrain, and which mitigations are on.

**Where the spec and the prompt disagree, or the spec can't be met:**
- **Occlusion:** the spec asks for GPU culling against a depth pyramid with indirect draws, two-phase. WebGL2 has neither compute shaders nor indirect draws. I built a conservative CPU version instead: a terrain horizon map per batching job, which only hides trees the terrain blocks from every camera position within 9 m. A brute-force check of thousands of culled trees found no wrong culls. It doesn't account for trees hiding other trees.
- **Prepass:** the spec requires it on, but on the Radeon 890M it costs about 1 ms more on average because the sprite pass is partly vertex-bound. It's kept for the 1% low.
- **Active-set reading:** I read "within its hysteresis margin" as near the actual switching point. Read literally (anywhere in the 15% band), you'd get about 3,000 active trees.
- **Fade cap vs. active count:** with 32 fades of 0.3 s, at most ~107 trees can change level per second. On a dense stage more cross than that, and trees waiting for a slot have to stay active. That is a large part of the remaining ~370.
- **The 1 ms GPU budget can't be met with the spec's thresholds.** The cost is the volume of foliage sprites (about 2M per frame). Bringing the thresholds closer, which `Lod.budget` allows for lower quality settings, gave 15.4 ms average at half distance and 10.4 ms at 0.3×, still not 1 ms. These two runs were on the old timing, so compare them with b7's 38 ms, not b8. Changing medium's thresholds is your call, so I left them alone.
- **Tree load is 0.6 s against 0.5 s,** because no variants came from the cache (0 of 24) during these runs. I didn't change that here.
